description: Initial lazy-root benchmark harness compile failed because Nickel Context::eval_shallow() returns NickelError directly; added plan to map NickelError into local benchmark Error before rerunning.

Initial lazy-root autoresearch harness: added wide checked-in fixture, shallow discovery benchmark, eager selected-root baseline, and checks. Baseline medians show selected_root_total_wall_ns=72.4ms with current eager path forcing all 128 roots.

Selected-root force now uses a wrapper evaluation of only the requested record field instead of eager all-root extraction. Benchmark counts drop from 128/127 to 1/0 and selected_root_total_wall_ns improves from 72.4ms to 64.3ms while all_roots_total_wall_ns guardrail stays 38.9ms.

Reused one Nickel Context across discovery and selected-root force by importing the fixture through a synthetic session source. Selected_root_force_wall_ns dropped from 32.2ms to 0.27ms while discovery stayed ~32.7ms; selected_root_total_wall_ns improved from 64.3ms to 33.0ms with counts still 1/0.

Confirmation rerun of the shared-Context wrapper benchmark. Same code reproduced the big win: selected_root_total_wall_ns nudged from 32.98ms to 32.87ms, keeping discovery ~32.5ms and selected_root_force_wall_ns under 0.30ms.

Tried nickel-lang-core Program-backed discovery and selected-root forcing. Big regression: selected_root_total_wall_ns jumped to 127.7ms and discovery alone to 126.7ms, so Program::query/eval_full_for_export is much heavier than the current Context+wrapper path for this workload.

Tried refining the nickel-lang-core path to use Program::parse() for syntactic top-level record labels plus Program field selection for selected-root force. It crashed before benchmarking: Program::parse() panicked inside nickel-lang-core with `File parsed and then immediately accessed doesn't exist`, so this path is not stable enough for the loop.

Tried replacing eval_shallow-based discovery with wrapper `std.record.fields(import fixture)` via eval_deep_for_export, while moving benchmark/check scripts to a disk-backed CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Discovery regressed badly: root_discovery_wall_ns rose from ~32.5ms to 42.6ms and selected_root_total_wall_ns to 43.1ms, so deep export of field names defeats the shared-Context win even though force still stayed under 0.5ms.

Tried discovering root labels from the already-read fixture source string with Context::eval_shallow(source) while still forcing the selected root via the import-wrapper path. Mixed result: discovery improved to 31.6ms, but selected_root_force_wall_ns regressed to 3.47ms, so losing the old import-cache reuse made selected_root_total_wall_ns land at 35.2ms instead of the 32.9ms best.

Tried keeping the shallow root record alive and forcing only the selected field with Context::eval_expr_shallow before direct to_serde deserialization. Nickel only reduced the field to WHNF: CrunchDerivation deserialization failed with `invalid type: Other, expected: String`, so at least one derivation field still needs recursive forcing beyond a single shallow step.

Prototype public-API fast path: reuse one shallow root record, then lazily force only the selected derivation and manually decode simple string/array fields. It improved selected_root_total_wall_ns to 32.31ms with selected_root_force_wall_ns down to 0.20ms, but the implementation only handled the benchmark fixture shape (no env/inputs/fixed_output/provenance) inside example support, so it is not general enough to keep yet.

Generalized the fast path into production seams: `crunch_eval::ShallowRecordSession` now keeps one shallow top-level record alive, and `crunch_glue::decode_crunch_derivation_lazy()` recursively forces only the selected derivation fields. Benchmark improved from 32.87ms to 32.32ms total with selected_root_force_wall_ns down to 0.19ms, while new tests cover bad siblings plus nested env/inputs/fixed_output/provenance so the win is not fixture-only.

Added `ShallowRecordSession::scan_for_label()` so selected-root discovery can scan the shallow top-level record for count+target presence without allocating owned label strings on the hot path. Benchmark improved from 32.32ms to 31.97ms total while preserving root_count=128, selected-label validation, and the same lazy selected-root force path.

Made `ShallowRecordSession::scan_for_label()` use the shallow record’s O(1)-style metadata path (`len()` plus direct field lookup) instead of iterating every top-level field. That keeps the selected-root discovery API general while dropping selected_root_total_wall_ns from 31.97ms to 31.25ms and root_discovery_wall_ns to 31.06ms on the same 128-root fixture.

Tried fusing discovery and selection into one `scan_and_select_field()` helper so benchmark path could reuse the selected Expr instead of looking it up twice. First compile failed because the new `SelectedTopLevelField` derived `Debug`, but `nickel_lang::Expr` is not `Debug`; fix is trivial, then rerun to measure whether the saved lookup matters.

Tried fusing discovery and selection into one `scan_and_select_field()` helper so the benchmark could reuse the selected Expr and skip a second lookup. Big regression: cloning the selected field Expr during discovery was much more expensive than the cheap presence probe, pushing selected_root_total_wall_ns to 53.9ms and root_discovery_wall_ns to 53.4ms.

Added `ShallowRecordSession::field_count()` and stopped re-checking selected-label presence during discovery. The selected-root path now counts top-level roots in discovery and lets the force step own selected-field lookup, which dropped selected_root_total_wall_ns from 31.25ms to 30.42ms and root_discovery_wall_ns to 30.24ms without changing force counts or the 128-root guardrail.

Tried pre-scanning derivation records into a `DerivationFieldExprs` struct so lazy decode could trade repeated named lookups for one iterator pass. It regressed badly: selected_root_total_wall_ns rose to 32.38ms and selected_root_force_wall_ns to 0.23ms, so the extra top-level iteration and field collection cost more than the old direct lookups on this workload.

Tried caching `nickel_lang::Record` handles through lazy derivation decode so the hot path would avoid repeated `Expr::as_record()` calls and named-lookups would share one borrowed record view. It regressed to 32.98ms total and 0.22ms selected-force, so the extra wrapper plumbing and record-handle threading cost more than the old direct helper calls.

Tried precomputing a reusable `ShallowRecordSessionConfig` so repeated benchmark samples could skip re-deriving source-name and import-path metadata before each `eval_shallow`. It regressed to 32.69ms total and 32.48ms discovery, so cloning the prepared config each sample was slower than rebuilding those tiny path-derived values inline.

Tried caching top-level field count inside `ShallowRecordSession` so discovery would avoid a second `as_record().len()` after `eval_shallow`. It regressed badly to 43.34ms total and 43.05ms discovery; whatever borrow/layout/codegen change that added around session construction outweighed the saved lookup, so keep field_count computed on demand.

Tried making `ShallowRecordSession::field_count()` and `scan_for_label()` infallible now that the session constructor already validates top-level roots. That should have been a pure API/codegen cleanup, but benchmark cratered to 122.3ms total and 121.4ms discovery, so this reshaping clearly hurt optimized codegen on the hot path and is not worth keeping.

Tried a general simple-derivation fast path in `decode_crunch_derivation_lazy()` that detects absent complex fields (`env`/`inputs`/`fixed_output`/`provenance`) and decodes simple roots through direct `Record` lookups before falling back. It cratered to 73.10ms total and 72.44ms discovery, so the extra branch/helper layer hurt codegen far more than it saved on the benchmark’s simple derivations.

Tried adding `#[inline]` hints on hot `ShallowRecordSession` and lazy-derivation decode helpers to encourage cross-crate inlining across the benchmark path. It still regressed from 30.42ms to 31.18ms total, so the compiler’s default inlining choices were better than the forced hints here.

Baseline re-measurement at session start. Current best code from prior session (field_count + no redundant label check). selected_root_total=32.97ms, discovery=32.77ms, force=0.20ms. Prior session best was 30.42ms median — variance is expected across sessions.

asi.bottleneck: discovery is 99.4% of total — almost entirely Nickel eval_shallow cost
asi.force_status: 0.20ms is negligible, no room to optimize
asi.nickel_api: eval_shallow is the cheapest Nickel API (WHNF only), can't go lower
asi.prior_dead_ends: inline hints, caching field_count, precomputing config, fusing scan+select, DerivationFieldExprs pre-scan, Record handle caching — all regressed
asi.remaining_angles: Context::new() overhead isolation, import_paths Vec allocation, source_name String allocation, reduce fixture-independent per-session overhead, profile parsing vs VM eval split

description: Implemented isolated-worker bounded root forcing, streamed pipeline eval/convert into the worker, added parallel all-root benchmark coverage and captured the first parallel_all_roots_total_wall_ns baseline bundle for the wide fixture.

Tried reducing parallel all-root overhead by reusing one isolated session per worker chunk instead of reopening a session per label. Benchmark run crashed before measurement because Cargo target dir `target/autoresearch-parallel-root` became unusable (`quote` failed with `E0463: can't find crate proc_macro2`) after prior test/build reuse.

Reduced bounded parallel all-root overhead by reusing one isolated EvaluationSession per worker chunk instead of reopening a worker session per label. Also switched autoresearch to fresh per-run Cargo target dirs to avoid shared-target corruption and benchmark contamination.

Reused coordinator-discovered root shape and labels inside IsolatedWorkerInput so worker sessions skip repeated shallow discovery before deep forcing. This trims bounded parallel all-root time slightly beyond the per-worker-session reuse change.

Tried pre-resolving requested labels to top-level indexes and skipping per-force label lookup inside worker sessions. That extra assignment/index plumbing regressed parallel_all_roots_total_wall_ns badly (281.6ms vs 113.4ms), so revert and keep the simpler worker-chunk session reuse design.

Applied the coordinator-derived worker metadata to the actual bounded parallel path: force_worker_assignment now opens worker sessions from cached shape+labels via open_worker_source instead of re-running shallow discovery in each worker. This removes redundant per-worker discovery before deep forcing.

Shrank worker-session label metadata to each worker chunk's requested subset instead of cloning the full discovered root-label list into every worker session. This keeps the cached shape reuse but trims per-worker label cloning and lookup work.

Tried reducing worker-input clone cost by converting session/worker source metadata to Arc-backed shared state (`Arc<str>`, `Arc<[OsString]>`, `Arc<[RootLabel]>`). The benchmark command crashed before measurement with a transient Cargo build failure (`can't find crate for gix_odb` / `fuse_backend_rs`) while compiling vendor dependencies into a fresh target dir.

Hypothesis: Arc-back shared IsolatedWorkerInput metadata (source/import_paths/source_name/labels) would cut worker-input clone cost across bounded parallel all-roots. Result: compile-path transient gone, but benchmark still regressed to 109.5ms vs 108.3ms best, so clone savings do not beat Arc conversion/to_vec overhead on worker-session open. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: leave worker metadata owned/simple and look at chunk scheduling or per-root deep-force costs instead.

Hypothesis: avoid full per-worker deep export by deep-evaluating only the selected top-level field through a new `Context::eval_expr_deep_for_export` helper in Nickel, reusing one worker shallow top-level expr. Crash: crunch-eval depends on crates.io `nickel-lang` 2.0.0 here, not the edited vendored source, so the new helper was invisible at compile time; worker error plumbing also tried `to_string()` on raw `nickel_lang::Error`. Rollback reason: experiment could not compile. Next action hint: use only existing public Nickel APIs in crunch-eval, or patch dependency source first before trying new Context methods.

Hypothesis: add adaptive serial fallback for bounded selected/all-root forcing when each worker chunk would be tiny, so small jobs avoid thread/session overhead and reuse one deep-export session. Crash: first cut mismatched the current Arc-backed `open_worker_source` signature and failed to compile with `expected Arc<[OsString]>` / `expected Arc<str>`. Rollback reason: compile error in fallback helper. Next action hint: keep the fallback idea but match the live worker-input types, then rerun.

Hypothesis: bounded root forcing should fall back to one serial worker session when each worker chunk is tiny (chunk_len <= 4), avoiding thread/session overhead on small jobs like the 16-root wide fixture at concurrency=4. Result regressed badly to 117.6ms vs 108.3ms best, so the serial fallback lost more than it saved under the current Arc-backed worker-input path. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep bounded parallel dispatch for this workload and inspect why the serial helper path is slower than the existing eager-all-roots guardrail before trying more routing heuristics.

Hypothesis: retest the tiny-chunk serial fallback on the real owned String/Vec worker metadata instead of the discarded Arc-backed variant, so small bounded jobs reuse one session without the Arc regression. Crash: first rebase back to owned worker metadata still left one `force_worker_assignment` call site passing owned clones into the restored `&[OsString]` / `&str` `open_worker_source` signature. Rollback reason: compile error from incomplete type rollback. Next action hint: finish the owned-worker rollback consistently, then rerun the serial-fallback measurement.

Switched bounded worker fan-out from `std::thread::spawn` to `std::thread::scope`, letting worker closures borrow the shared worker input instead of cloning it into `'static` threads. This dropped parallel_all_roots_total_wall_ns from the prior 108.3ms best to 106.6ms on the 16-root fixture; eager all-roots guardrail stayed healthy at 61.6ms and selected-root force counts remained 1/0.

Hypothesis: after switching to scoped threads, worker results already arrive in request order, so removing per-chunk label Vec clones and the final result sort should trim bounded fan-out overhead. Result cratered to 126.0ms vs 106.6ms best; the borrowed-slice/lifetime reshaping clearly hurt codegen more than it saved in tiny result handling. Rollback reason: much worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the simpler owned WorkerAssignment/result structs and look elsewhere, likely around session open or thread launch itself rather than final ordering bookkeeping.

Capped effective worker count so bounded forcing keeps at least 8 requested roots per worker before fanning out, which trims redundant whole-session worker setup on small root sets while still honoring the caller's upper concurrency bound. On the 16-root fixture this reduces effective workers from 4 to 2 and improves parallel_all_roots_total_wall_ns from 106.64ms to 106.21ms; selected-root counts stayed 1/0 and eager all-roots guardrail stayed healthy at 62.9ms.

Hypothesis: once effective worker count is clamped, worker hot path can skip a second string lookup by forcing roots from already-selected `RootLabel`s instead of calling `session.force_root(label)` and re-searching `session.labels`. Crash: first cut moved `worker_labels` into `open_worker_source` and then tried to iterate it again, so borrow checker rejected the worker loop. Rollback reason: compile error from ownership mistake in the known-label path. Next action hint: either iterate over `session.root_labels()` after session construction or clone only the small selected label vector before moving it.

Hypothesis: keep the known-RootLabel fast path but iterate the worker session’s own selected labels, so worker hot path avoids repeated string lookup without extra plumbing. Crash: borrowing `session.root_labels()` for iteration conflicts with the mutable borrow needed for `force_root_with_known_label`, so the compiler rejected the loop. Rollback reason: mutable/immutable borrow conflict in the worker loop. Next action hint: clone the small selected label vector once after session construction, then reuse those owned `RootLabel`s for the known-label force path.

Hypothesis: after worker-count clamping, preselected worker labels should drive forcing directly through a `force_root_with_known_label` helper, avoiding repeated `session.force_root(label)` linear scans over the small selected label set. Result cratered to 126.3ms vs 106.2ms best; cloning the selected labels once and reshaping the helper path hurt codegen far more than the tiny lookup cost. Rollback reason: much worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the plain string-label worker loop and focus on bigger overheads than per-root label lookup.

Hypothesis: raise `MIN_ROOTS_PER_WORKER` from 8 to 16 so the 16-root workload collapses to one worker, cutting one more whole-session deep-eval and thread launch from the bounded path. Result regressed slightly to 106.97ms vs 106.21ms best, so one-worker routing is a bit worse than the current two-worker clamp on this fixture. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the 8-roots-per-worker clamp and probe other worker-setup overheads instead of pushing all the way to one worker.

Hypothesis: tune the minimum-roots-per-worker clamp from 8 down to 6 so the 16-root workload uses 3 workers instead of 2, which might better balance redundant worker setup against available parallelism. Result regressed to 111.16ms vs 106.21ms best, so 3 workers are clearly worse than the current 2-worker clamp on this fixture. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the 8-root threshold; the local search now shows 1 worker slower, 3 workers slower, and 2 workers best so far.

Hypothesis: after switching to scoped threads, the old Arc-backed worker/session metadata may no longer help and owned String/Vec fields could give better codegen than Arc conversions. Result regressed to 108.02ms vs 106.21ms best, so the current Arc-backed metadata is still slightly better in the scoped+clamped path on this fixture. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the Arc-backed session metadata and probe other overheads instead of reverting that earlier reshape.

Hypothesis: specialize `force_all_roots_bounded` so the primary workload sends contiguous `RootLabel` chunks directly to workers instead of cloning a full `Vec<String>` and re-selecting labels by string before every worker session. Result exploded to 316.5ms vs 106.2ms best, so the dedicated all-roots worker path hurt codegen or duplicated enough setup to swamp the saved string-selection work. Rollback reason: catastrophically worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the shared selected-root worker machinery even for all-roots; the extra specialization is not worth it on this path.

Hypothesis: scoped workers already join in assignment order, so the final sort over `IndexedRoot.index` should be redundant and removable. Result regressed slightly to 106.83ms vs 106.21ms best, and the change also left an `IndexedRoot.index` warning behind, so the explicit sort is not worth touching here. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the current sort-and-index bookkeeping and search for a larger win than this tiny tail cleanup.

Hypothesis: session open still re-runs a full top-level `eval_shallow` during discovery, so deriving labels directly from the already-available `shallow_expr` from `open_source` should cut discovery overhead for the parallel benchmark. Result regressed badly to 152.78ms vs 106.21ms best, so this refactor hurt optimized codegen or invalidated a beneficial sharing path instead of saving work. Rollback reason: much worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the existing discovery flow; the duplicate-looking top-level shallow evaluation is apparently cheaper than this reshaped label-discovery helper path.

Hypothesis: with the current 2-worker clamp, one assignment can run on the caller thread while only the remaining assignments spawn helper threads, saving one spawn/join pair on the hot path. Result cratered to 273.39ms vs 106.21ms best, so this mixed local+spawn scheduling reshaped the hot path badly enough to swamp the saved spawn cost. Rollback reason: catastrophically worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the simpler all-scoped-worker fan-out; thread-count savings need a different design than this local-worker split.

Hypothesis: collect syscall-level evidence for the current best code by stracing the benchmark binary directly before more code changes. Crash: autoresearch harness rejected the command because this repo requires experiments to run through `./autoresearch.sh`, not custom benchmark invocations. Rollback reason: harness policy rejection, no code change measured. Next action hint: if more profiling evidence is needed, wrap the profiling tool around `./autoresearch.sh` itself or use non-experiment shell commands outside the autoresearch runner.

Hypothesis: worker threads are tiny and short-lived, so spawning them with a much smaller stack via `Builder::spawn_scoped(...).stack_size(512 KiB)` might trim spawn overhead and memory pressure. Result cratered to 233.63ms vs 106.21ms best, so custom builder-based spawning is far worse here than plain scoped-thread spawning. Rollback reason: catastrophically worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep default scoped-thread spawning; the builder path adds too much overhead on this hot path.

Hypothesis: for record-shaped root sets, each worker can wrap the original source into a smaller record containing only its assigned labels, so `eval_deep_for_export` forces only that subset instead of all roots in every worker session. Result cratered to 247.32ms vs 106.21ms best; the wrapper-source generation and Nickel field-projection path are far worse than the current full-source worker sessions on this fixture. Rollback reason: catastrophically worse primary metric. Next action hint: drop the wrapper-source idea from the hot path unless Nickel exposes a real per-expression deep-export API.

Hypothesis: patch crunch to use the vendored `nickel-lang`, add `Context::eval_expr_deep_for_export`, and change worker forcing to deep-export only each selected top-level field from one shallow worker expr instead of `eval_deep_for_export(full_source)` per worker. Result cratered to 267.89ms vs 106.21ms best, so this per-field deep-export path is much slower than the existing whole-session deep-export worker path on the wide fixture even when the API is available. Rollback reason: catastrophically worse primary metric. Next action hint: drop this path for now; remaining wins likely need thread reuse or different Nickel internals, not per-field export through the current public wrapper.

Hypothesis: once bounded forcing clamps to only 2 effective workers on the 16-root fixture, `force_all_roots_bounded` should bypass the isolated-worker path entirely and reuse the coordinator session’s eager `force_all_roots()` fast path, eliminating duplicate worker deep exports. Result still regressed badly to 138.34ms vs 106.21ms best, so this adaptive serial handoff does not inherit the standalone eager-all-roots guardrail cost the way expected. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep bounded all-roots on the current isolated-worker machinery; the eager serial path is not a drop-in win inside this API boundary.

Hypothesis: replace per-call scoped thread spawning with cached Rayon thread pools keyed by effective bounded concurrency, so repeated benchmark samples reuse worker threads instead of paying OS-thread spawn/join each call. Result cratered to 244.36ms vs 106.21ms best, so this Rayon pool path adds far more scheduling/abstraction overhead than it saves on the current worker workload. Rollback reason: catastrophically worse primary metric. Next action hint: drop external pool abstraction here; if thread reuse matters, it likely needs a much thinner purpose-built path.

Hypothesis: for the common 2-worker-clamped all-roots case, do one coordinator deep export and deserialize each extracted root through JSON instead of paying one whole-program deep export per worker. Crash: first cut borrowed `self` through `ensure_deep_expr()` while also mutating `forced_root_count`, so the compiler rejected the helper with E0503/E0506. Rollback reason: borrow-check failure in the coordinator JSON path. Next action hint: clone or otherwise detach the deep expr before the per-root loop, then rerun the single-deep-export experiment.

Hypothesis: for the common 2-worker-clamped all-roots case, do one coordinator deep export and deserialize each extracted root through JSON instead of paying one whole-program deep export per worker. Result still regressed badly to 153.58ms vs 106.21ms best, so the extra JSON export/parse path costs more than the duplicated worker deep exports it removes on this fixture. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: drop coordinator JSON deserialization as an optimization path; any single-deep-export design likely needs a much cheaper intermediate than JSON.

Hypothesis: replace per-call scoped thread spawning with a very thin custom persistent worker pool built from std channels and long-lived threads, avoiding the heavy Rayon abstraction that regressed earlier. Crash: first cut hit `E0310` because job results crossing the persistent pool threads need `T: 'static` on the pool submission path. Rollback reason: compile error from missing lifetime bound in the custom pool helper. Next action hint: add the explicit `'static` bound where the job result crosses the worker-thread boundary, then rerun the thin custom-pool experiment.

Replaced per-call scoped worker spawning with a very thin custom persistent bounded worker pool built from std channels and long-lived threads. Unlike the earlier Rayon pool, this keeps scheduling overhead minimal while reusing worker threads across the benchmark’s repeated bounded calls. parallel_all_roots_total_wall_ns improved from 106.21ms to 105.37ms; selected-root counts stayed 1/0 and eager all-roots guardrail stayed healthy at 64.1ms.

Hypothesis: with the new custom persistent worker pool, wrapping the shared worker input in one outer `Arc` and cloning that per assignment might cut per-job metadata cloning further than cloning `IsolatedWorkerInput` directly. Result regressed badly to 117.63ms vs 105.37ms best, so the extra outer `Arc` indirection is worse than the existing direct clone path. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the simple `IsolatedWorkerInput` clone per job and avoid layering more pointer indirection onto the hot path.

Tightened the custom persistent worker pool by switching both job delivery and result delivery to bounded `sync_channel(1)` queues. The bounded all-roots path only has one outstanding job/result per worker at a time, so the simpler bounded queue path trims channel overhead without changing semantics. parallel_all_roots_total_wall_ns improved from 105.37ms to 104.88ms; selected-root counts stayed 1/0 and eager all-roots guardrail remained healthy.

Hypothesis: the bounded worker pool does not need atomic round-robin selection on this hot path because assignments are submitted serially; directly targeting worker slots from the caller should shave a little pool bookkeeping. Result regressed to 106.75ms vs 104.88ms best and also introduced warnings from the now-unused generic submit path, so the extra submit helper split is not worth it. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the simpler atomic round-robin submit path; sender-slot selection is not the bottleneck.

Hypothesis: the custom persistent worker pool may be even cheaper with rendezvous job delivery (`sync_channel(0)`) because workers are already parked waiting for the next bounded task, so no one-item job buffer is needed. Result regressed to 106.09ms vs 104.88ms best, so forcing sender/worker rendezvous is a bit worse than the current one-slot buffered job queue. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the one-slot buffered job queue; it seems to smooth worker handoff better than strict rendezvous.

Hypothesis: after switching to the persistent bounded worker pool, the old 8-roots-per-worker clamp may be too conservative and the 16-root fixture might now benefit from reusing all 4 workers. Lowering `MIN_ROOTS_PER_WORKER` to 4 makes the benchmark use 4 workers again, but it regressed to 108.37ms vs 104.88ms best. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the clamp above 4; cheaper worker reuse does not make 4-way fan-out worthwhile on this workload.

Hypothesis: persistent worker reuse may make a 3-worker split best even if 4 workers and 1 worker were worse, so lowering `MIN_ROOTS_PER_WORKER` to 6 would retune the 16-root fixture to 3 workers. Result still regressed to 107.40ms vs 104.88ms best. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the current 8-root clamp; even after persistent worker reuse, the local search still says 2 workers beat both 3 and 4.

Hypothesis: the thin custom worker pool might get a little cheaper by swapping std `sync_channel(1)` for crossbeam bounded channels while keeping the same one-job/one-result semantics. Result regressed to 109.30ms vs 104.88ms best, so the extra dependency/abstraction does not beat std’s bounded channels on this tiny hot path. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep std bounded channels; channel implementation choice is no longer the main lever.

Hypothesis: current best workload clamps to 2 workers, so replacing `% self.senders.len()` with a tiny `next_worker_index()` fast path for 1- and 2-worker pools might shave round-robin submit overhead in the persistent pool. Result regressed to 110.78ms vs 104.88ms best, so the extra helper branching is worse than the plain modulo path here. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the simpler round-robin submit logic; sender-index arithmetic is not worth special-casing.

Hypothesis: the previous queue win may have come mostly from bounded job delivery, so keeping the worker job queue bounded while reverting the per-job result queue back to an unbounded channel might trim result-path overhead further. Result cratered to 273.82ms vs 104.88ms best, so the bounded one-slot result queue is clearly essential to the persistent pool win. Rollback reason: catastrophically worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep both job and result delivery bounded; mixed bounded/unbounded channels are a dead end here.

Hypothesis: test the other mixed queue variant by keeping the per-job result queue bounded but reverting the long-lived worker job queue to an unbounded channel, to see which queue side drives the persistent-pool win. Crash: first cut changed the worker channel constructor without changing the pool sender type, so the build failed with a `Sender` vs `SyncSender` mismatch. Rollback reason: compile error from incomplete mixed-queue change. Next action hint: if we still want this variant, change the pool sender type consistently and rerun; otherwise result from the opposite mixed variant already suggests mixed queues are probably a dead end.

Hypothesis: after the persistent worker-pool win, re-test the old 1-worker clamp because reduced thread overhead might make one whole-program deep export beat the current 2-worker split. Raising `MIN_ROOTS_PER_WORKER` to 16 makes the 16-root fixture use 1 worker again, but it still regressed to 106.35ms vs 104.88ms best. Rollback reason: worse primary metric. Next action hint: keep the 2-worker clamp; persistent worker reuse did not flip the old 1-vs-2 worker result.

Hypothesis: re-baseline current HEAD before new experiments. Runner invocation failed because autoresearch mode requires the checked-in harness entrypoint directly (`./autoresearch.sh` or `bash autoresearch.sh`), not a wrapped `cd && ...` command. Rollback reason: harness policy rejection, no benchmark data captured. Next action hint: rerun via `run_experiment` with command `./autoresearch.sh` from repo root.

asi.hypothesis: re-baseline current HEAD before new experiments
asi.rollback_reason: run_experiment rejected a wrapped command instead of executing the harness
asi.next_action_hint: rerun with command './autoresearch.sh' directly

description: Baseline re-measurement on current HEAD before new code changes. Current tree beats the prior recorded best slightly at 104.47ms vs 104.88ms, so keep this fresh benchmark anchor before trying further pool hot-path work.

asi.hypothesis: current HEAD may have a slightly different baseline and should be re-measured before new changes
asi.baseline_context: fresh session after preserving unrelated dirty worktree in stash@{0}
asi.next_action_hint: optimize custom worker-pool hot path from this clean baseline

description: Tried trimming bounded worker-pool overhead by replacing per-assignment label Vec clones with requested-label ranges and by using one shared result channel per execute call instead of one result channel per worker job. The combined refactor regressed the parallel all-roots benchmark from the fresh 104.47ms baseline to 109.97ms, so the old per-job receiver path was faster on this workload.

asi.hypothesis: range-based worker assignments plus a single shared collector channel would reduce small per-call allocation and channel overhead in force_all_roots_bounded
asi.rollback_reason: primary metric regressed by about 5.5ms versus the current baseline
asi.next_action_hint: revert this shared-result/range-assignment path and try a thinner worker request protocol or lower-risk instrumentation instead
asi.notes: Session tests still passed before the benchmark, so the loss is performance-only rather than a correctness regression.

description: Tried only the range-based assignment half of the prior refactor while keeping the existing per-job result receivers and round-robin pool submit path. Replacing chunk-owned label Vecs with requested-label index ranges still regressed the benchmark from the fresh 104.47ms baseline to 109.18ms, so the current chunk-owned assignment layout appears to help codegen more than it hurts allocations on this workload.

asi.hypothesis: removing per-assignment label Vec clones while preserving the existing per-job result channel path would shave bounded all-roots worker setup overhead
asi.rollback_reason: primary metric regressed by about 4.7ms versus the current baseline
asi.next_action_hint: keep the current chunk-owned WorkerAssignment shape and look for deeper worker-pool or Nickel-eval levers instead of assignment-layout refactors
asi.notes: Targeted session tests still passed before benchmarking, so the loss is again performance-only.

description: Tried specializing only the all-roots entry point so it builds the existing chunk-owned `WorkerAssignment { labels: Vec<String> }` directly from `RootLabel`s, avoiding the extra full-label Vec clone in `force_all_roots_with_policy` while leaving the worker-pool path unchanged. It still regressed the benchmark from the fresh 104.47ms baseline to 107.39ms, so even this mild all-roots-only specialization hurt optimized codegen more than the saved outer label clone helped.

asi.hypothesis: avoiding the extra all-roots label Vec clone while preserving the current worker-assignment and per-job result-channel path would trim bounded all-roots setup cost
asi.rollback_reason: primary metric regressed by about 2.9ms versus the current baseline
asi.next_action_hint: drop all-roots label-specialization ideas and focus on deeper worker-session or Nickel-eval costs instead of label cloning
asi.notes: The added helper-equivalence unit test and the existing session tests passed before the benchmark; the change was behavior-preserving but slower.

description: Tried keeping the current worker-pool structure but storing chunk-owned assignment labels in `SmallVec<[String; MIN_ROOTS_PER_WORKER]>` so the common 8-label chunks can stay inline instead of heap-allocating a Vec per assignment and assignment clone. That still regressed the benchmark from the fresh 104.47ms baseline to 108.82ms, so the heavier inline `SmallVec` layout hurt this hot path more than it saved in heap churn.

asi.hypothesis: inline smallvec storage for the common 8-label worker chunks would reduce heap allocation overhead without changing worker-pool behavior
asi.rollback_reason: primary metric regressed by about 4.35ms versus the current baseline
asi.next_action_hint: drop assignment-container micro-tuning and focus on deeper worker-session or Nickel evaluation costs
asi.notes: Relevant session tests still passed before the benchmark; the regression is performance-only.

description: Tried pre-warming worker sessions by calling `Context::eval_shallow()` inside `open_worker_source()` before the later `eval_deep_for_export()`, hoping the worker Context would reuse the same warm-path advantages the coordinator gets after `open_file()`. It regressed badly from the fresh 104.47ms baseline to 117.41ms, so worker `eval_shallow()` cost was additive rather than a helpful warm-up for worker deep export on this Nickel path.

asi.hypothesis: a worker-side shallow eval before deep export would warm Nickel context state and reduce per-worker deep-eval cost
asi.rollback_reason: primary metric regressed by about 12.94ms versus the current baseline
asi.next_action_hint: do not pre-warm worker contexts with eval_shallow; look for ways to avoid duplicate worker deep exports entirely or target other Nickel internals
asi.notes: Relevant session tests still passed before the benchmark, so the worker warm-up changed only performance, not correctness.

description: Tried a thinner threaded dispatch path that keeps the existing worker pool, result channels, and chunk-owned `WorkerAssignment { labels: Vec<String> }` layout but moves assignments into worker closures instead of cloning each assignment in the threaded executor. That still regressed the benchmark from the fresh 104.47ms baseline to 109.64ms, so even the per-assignment Vec<String> clone appears cheaper than the control-flow reshaping needed to avoid it.

asi.hypothesis: consuming worker assignments directly in the threaded path would cut hot-path label-clone overhead without revisiting the already-bad assignment-shape changes
asi.rollback_reason: primary metric regressed by about 5.17ms versus the current baseline
asi.next_action_hint: stop chasing WorkerAssignment clone elimination and move to deeper worker protocol or Nickel-boundary experiments
asi.notes: The relevant crunch-eval session tests still passed before benchmarking; this was another performance-only loss.

description: Tried a deeper Nickel-core worker path by adding a direct `nickel-lang-core` dependency and prototyping worker evaluation through `Program::new_from_source(...).eval_full_for_export()` instead of the public `Context` wrapper. The experiment failed before benchmarking because adding direct `nickel-lang-core = 0.16.1` pulled `topiary-core` and a conflicting `wasm-bindgen = 0.2.100`, which clashes with the workspace's existing `wasm-bindgen = 0.2.117` selection via reqwest/crunch-store.

asi.hypothesis: using nickel-lang-core Program directly in worker sessions might avoid the public Context path's repeated source-add overhead and reduce per-worker deep-export cost
asi.rollback_reason: workspace dependency resolution failed before the code could compile or benchmark
asi.next_action_hint: avoid a naive direct nickel-lang-core dependency bump; if pursuing core internals, inspect whether nickel-lang re-exports enough internals, use the exact transitive version/features already in the lockfile, or prototype in an isolated scratch crate first
asi.error_detail: wasm-bindgen version conflict between topiary-core's pinned 0.2.100 and workspace-selected 0.2.117

description: Retried the deeper Nickel-core worker idea with `nickel-lang-core = { default-features = false }` so the prototype could compile: worker assignments used `Program::new_from_source(...).eval_full_for_export()` plus direct core-value field extraction/deserialization instead of the public `Context` wrapper. It still regressed the benchmark from the fresh 104.47ms baseline to 109.51ms, so even without the earlier dependency-conflict baggage the core Program path is slower than the current public worker-session path on this workload.

asi.hypothesis: a minimal-feature nickel-lang-core Program path in worker sessions would avoid public Context source-add overhead and reduce per-worker deep-export cost
asi.rollback_reason: primary metric regressed by about 5.03ms versus the current baseline
asi.next_action_hint: drop the direct Program worker path; remaining wins likely need a truly thinner request/result protocol or a different Nickel internal seam than Program::eval_full_for_export
asi.notes: The focused crunch-eval session tests passed before benchmarking, so this was another behavior-preserving but slower deep-internal path.

description: Replace per-job result receivers with reusable per-worker result slots in the persistent bounded worker pool. Each worker now keeps a permanent result slot backed by a mutex/condvar while the existing boxed job closure and chunk-owned assignments stay unchanged, which removes the hot-path `sync_channel(1)` allocation on every submitted job without revisiting the label/container refactors that already regressed.

asi.hypothesis: reusable per-worker result slots would remove the remaining per-job result-channel allocation cost while preserving the worker pool, round-robin dispatch, and current assignment shape
asi.mechanism: BoundedWorkerPool now pairs each persistent worker thread with a reusable result slot; submit clears the slot, enqueues the boxed job, and collect_threaded_results waits on/takes the slot payload instead of allocating a fresh receiver per job
asi.kept_because: primary metric improved versus the fresh 104.47ms baseline while preserving the existing session tests
asi.next_action_hint: confirm the win with a no-code rerun and, if it holds, expose actual effective bounded concurrency in benchmark metrics so the measurement matches the clamp-to-2-worker behavior

description: Confirmation rerun after the reusable per-worker result-slot change. The same code improved again, from the previous 104.02ms result down to 101.65ms, which strengthens confidence that removing the per-job result-channel allocation was a real win and not a one-off noisy sample.

asi.hypothesis: the reusable per-worker result-slot change should continue to beat the old per-job receiver path on a fresh isolated rerun
asi.kept_because: same-code confirmation rerun improved further and raised confidence in the result
asi.next_action_hint: with the pool result-slot win confirmed, either expose actual effective bounded concurrency in benchmark metrics or attempt the harder boxed-job elimination separately without disturbing the new slot design

description: Tried the harder request-slot follow-up on top of the reusable result-slot win: replace boxed worker-job closures with a concrete `WorkerRequest` struct carrying the worker input, assignment, typed function pointer, and result slot, while keeping the new reusable result slots. This preserved behavior but regressed slightly from the confirmed 101.65ms best to 101.87ms, so boxed job closures are not the next hot-path bottleneck after the result-slot improvement.

asi.hypothesis: eliminating boxed worker-job closures with a concrete typed WorkerRequest protocol would stack another small win on top of reusable result slots
asi.rollback_reason: primary metric regressed by about 0.22ms versus the current best kept code
asi.next_action_hint: keep the reusable result-slot design but stop here on worker-protocol surgery; the next useful step is likely benchmark-metric accuracy (effective concurrency) or a different Nickel-level seam
asi.notes: Focused crunch-eval session tests still passed before benchmarking, so the change was behavior-preserving but slower.

description: Swap the reusable worker-result slots from `std::sync::{Mutex, Condvar}` to `parking_lot::{Mutex, Condvar}`. The result-slot design already removed per-job result receivers; using the lighter-weight parking_lot primitives trims the remaining lock/wake overhead on the hot path without changing the worker pool, assignment shape, or boxed-job protocol.

asi.hypothesis: parking_lot mutex/condvar primitives would make the kept reusable result-slot design cheaper than the std synchronization path
asi.kept_because: primary metric improved materially versus the confirmed 101.65ms kept result while preserving the focused session tests
asi.next_action_hint: confirm the parking_lot win with a rerun; if it holds, the remaining nearby improvement is likely metric/reporting accuracy rather than more worker-protocol surgery

description: Confirmation rerun of the parking_lot result-slot change did not reproduce the big first-sample win. The same code landed back at 104.53ms, essentially on top of the old 104.47ms baseline and far above the 99.50ms outlier, so the apparent parking_lot gain is not yet trustworthy.

asi.hypothesis: if parking_lot is a real improvement over std sync for result slots, a fresh rerun of the same code should stay clearly below the old ~101.65ms and baseline ~104.47ms levels
asi.rollback_reason: same-code confirmation rerun lost the initial win and landed near baseline, so the change is not yet proven beneficial
asi.next_action_hint: benchmark an explicit revert of the parking_lot change against the committed version before treating it as a durable optimization
asi.notes: No code changes were pending during the confirmation rerun; this is pure measurement evidence against over-trusting the first low sample.

description: Revert the parking_lot swap and restore the reusable result-slot implementation to `std::sync::{Mutex, Condvar}`. The parking_lot version produced one strong outlier but failed its no-code confirmation rerun; explicitly restoring the std sync path improved the metric from that confirmed 104.53ms level down to 103.10ms, which is a better fit for a durable result than keeping the noisy parking_lot variant.

asi.hypothesis: if the parking_lot win was noise, restoring the previous std sync result-slot path should beat the confirmed parking_lot rerun and recover a more trustworthy latency level
asi.kept_because: explicitly reverting the unconfirmed parking_lot change improved the metric relative to the confirmed parking_lot rerun while preserving focused session tests
asi.next_action_hint: confirm the std-sync revert with another no-code rerun; if it stays near or below ~103ms, keep std sync and move on to measurement accuracy or a new seam

description: Confirmation rerun after reverting the noisy parking_lot variant. The restored std-sync result-slot path improved again, from 103.10ms down to 102.28ms, which strengthens the case that the std-sync reusable result-slot design is the trustworthy post-confirmation winner and the earlier parking_lot low sample was noise.

asi.hypothesis: the explicit std-sync revert should keep beating the confirmed parking_lot rerun if the parking_lot win was noise
asi.kept_because: same-code confirmation rerun improved again and stayed clearly below the confirmed parking_lot rerun
asi.next_action_hint: with the result-slot design stabilized, either expose effective bounded concurrency in benchmark output or move to a genuinely new seam outside worker result plumbing

description: Tried removing the per-submit result-slot clear step now that the pool schedules at most one job per worker per call and every call drains all slots before returning. The change preserved behavior in the focused session tests but regressed from the current 102.28ms best to 103.54ms, so the explicit clear remains the better shape on this hot path.

asi.hypothesis: skipping the redundant-looking result-slot clear would shave one mutex lock/unlock per submitted worker job
asi.rollback_reason: primary metric regressed by about 1.26ms versus the current best kept code
asi.next_action_hint: keep the current result-slot clear and shift away from more result-slot micro-tuning toward measurement accuracy or a new higher-level seam
asi.notes: The edit also introduced an unused-method warning because `clear()` became dead code; the warning disappeared again after rollback.

description: No-code confirmation rerun on the current std-sync reusable result-slot path. This isolated rerun landed much slower at 108.78ms versus the earlier 102.28ms confirmation, so the current benchmark remains noisy enough that we should avoid over-trusting single low samples and keep looking for changes that beat the baseline more decisively.

asi.hypothesis: the current reusable result-slot implementation might hold near the recent ~102ms confirmations on another isolated rerun
asi.rollback_reason: same-code rerun regressed sharply and did not confirm the earlier low sample range
asi.next_action_hint: prefer changes with larger margins than the current noise band, or improve measurement fidelity (for example effective concurrency reporting) before trusting another tiny micro-win
asi.notes: There were no code changes in this run; the result is pure measurement evidence about the current noise envelope.

description: Tried exposing actual effective bounded concurrency in the benchmark outputs by adding an `effective_bounded_root_concurrency()` helper on `EvaluationSession` and wiring both benchmark entrypoints to record the clamped worker count instead of the configured concurrency. This unexpectedly cratered the primary metric from the current ~102ms region to 171.94ms, so even this seemingly harmless measurement-fidelity plumbing perturbed the hot path enough to reject for now.

asi.hypothesis: recording actual effective bounded concurrency would improve benchmark fidelity without materially changing the measured runtime
asi.rollback_reason: primary metric regressed catastrophically despite the change being intended as measurement-only plumbing
asi.next_action_hint: do not mix benchmark-reporting tweaks into the hot path casually; if we revisit metric fidelity, isolate it much more carefully or measure it outside the benchmarked region
asi.notes: Focused crunch-eval session tests still passed before the run, so the failure was purely benchmark performance.

description: Reuse the coordinator session inside `force_all_roots_bounded()` for small all-root sets instead of cloning the whole request into isolated workers. On the fixed 16-root fixture the bounded path previously paid two redundant full-program deep exports; the new small-set fallback collapses the primary metric from 102.28ms to 65.43ms and brings bounded all-roots back down to the eager all-roots cost envelope.

asi.hypothesis: for small all-root sets whose effective bounded fan-out is only one or two workers, reusing the existing session's in-process all-roots path would beat isolated worker sessions because the worker path duplicates whole-program deep export work
asi.kept_because: the primary metric improved massively and the guardrails stayed healthy: discovery remained ~47.11ms, selected-root stayed ~65.35ms with force counts 1/0, and eager all-roots stayed ~64.97ms
asi.mechanism: force_all_roots_bounded()/force_all_roots_with_policy() now compute effective bounded concurrency and reuse self.force_all_roots() for small all-root sets instead of routing through isolated worker sessions
asi.next_action_hint: the remaining primary-metric ceiling is now session open/root discovery, so future experiments should target cheaper open_file/discovery work or only revisit reporting for the now-misleading concurrency metric outside the hot path

description: No-code confirmation rerun of the small-set coordinator-session fallback. The same code improved again from 65.43ms to 64.08ms, confirming that the bounded all-roots path now reliably tracks the eager all-roots cost envelope on the fixed 16-root fixture instead of paying the old duplicated worker deep-export penalty.

asi.hypothesis: if the new small-set all-roots fallback is a real structural win, a fresh isolated rerun of the same code should stay near the new ~65ms band rather than bouncing back toward the old ~102ms worker-path band
asi.kept_because: same-code confirmation rerun stayed in the new low band and improved slightly again
asi.mechanism: no code change; this run purely confirmed the already-landed session-reuse routing inside force_all_roots_bounded()
asi.next_action_hint: treat the worker duplication problem as solved for the current fixture and shift future experiments toward open_file/discovery costs or out-of-band reporting of the now-misleading concurrency metric

description: Parse the source once to discover safe top-level static record labels and skip the expensive shallow Nickel evaluation during session open when the file is obviously a let-wrapped record package set. On the fixed wide fixture that collapses root discovery from about 47ms to 1.75ms and pulls the primary metric down from 64.08ms to 59.55ms without changing the later deep-export semantics.

asi.hypothesis: a parse-only static record-label fast path for clearly syntactic top-level package-set records would remove most open_file/discovery cost without changing force-time behavior
asi.kept_because: the primary metric improved materially and the guardrails stayed healthy: discovery dropped to ~1.75ms, selected-root total improved to ~58.44ms with force counts 1/0, and eager all-roots improved to ~60.61ms
asi.mechanism: open_source() now tries discover_static_record_labels() first; when parsing proves the source is a safe static top-level record without a top-level name field, the session seeds Record labels directly and skips eval_shallow/discover_roots
asi.next_action_hint: confirm this parse-only discovery fast path with a no-code rerun, then revisit the remaining dominant cost in selected_root_force / deep export rather than more discovery work
